chunks.text: Large language models can classify titles and abstracts with zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies according to predefined eligibility criteria.
Human oversight remains important for rigorous quality control, reproducibility, cost management and prompt refinement.
The experiment compared standard input-output prompting, zero-shot chain of thought, few-shot chain of thought and majority voting.
Recall was 0.82 for input-output, 0.97 for zero-shot chain of thought, and 1.0 for few-shot chain of thought and majority voting.
Majority voting improves robustness by reducing stochastic variability, but it requires multiple LLM calls and therefore increases cost and latency.
